root_cause.text: The NPU_SET_IFM_REGION command handler uses an incorrect bitmask (0x7f instead of 0x7) to extract the region index, allowing values up to 127 to be stored in a field that is later used as an array subscript into fixed-size arrays (region_size[] and output_region[]) dimensioned to only 8 elements, causing out-of-bounds heap writes.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that NPU_SET_IFM_REGION extracted the region index with `param & 0x7f` (line 467 in the original code), producing values 0-127, while the struct ethosu_validated_cmdstream_info arrays are sized to NPU_BASEP_REGION_MAX (8 elements, valid indices 0-7). All other region assignments in the same switch statement correctly use `param & 0x7`. The CVE description confirms that `feat_matrix_length()` and `calc_sizes()` use this region index directly as an array subscript: `info->region_size[fm->region]`, enabling a write up to 127*8 = 1016 bytes past the allocated buffer when a userspace caller supplies a param value > 7.

intent_record.intent_summary: Correct the IFM region bitmask from 0x7f to 0x7 to properly constrain the region field to its valid 3-bit range.
intent_record.what: Changed the bitmask for IFM region assignment from 0x7f (127 in decimal, 7 bits set) to 0x7 (7 in decimal, 3 bits set) on line 467.
intent_record.how: This change restricts the IFM region value to only the lower 3 bits instead of the lower 7 bits. Any region parameter value will now be masked to a maximum of 7 instead of 127, effectively limiting valid region indices to 0-7 instead of 0-127.

grouping_result.intent: Correct the IFM region bitmask from 0x7f to 0x7 to properly constrain the region field to its valid 3-bit range.

relevance_review.reason: This group directly addresses the root cause by correcting the bitmask used to extract the region index in the NPU_SET_IFM_REGION command handler. Changing the bitmask from 0x7f to 0x7 constrains the region field to valid 3-bit values (0-7), preventing out-of-bounds array access into the fixed-size arrays (region_size[] and output_region[]) that are dimensioned to 8 elements.

candidates.rationale: This statement uses the incorrect bitmask 0x7f (127 in decimal) instead of 0x7 (7 in decimal) to extract the region index. Since the region field is later used as an array subscript into fixed-size arrays dimensioned to only 8 elements (indices 0-7), allowing values up to 127 causes out-of-bounds heap writes. The correct mask 0x7 would constrain the value to the valid 3-bit range (0-7).

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement uses an incorrect bitmask (0x7f) to extract the region index from the NPU_SET_IFM_REGION command parameter. The mask 0x7f allows values 0-127 to be stored in st.ifm.region, but this field is subsequently used as an array subscript into fixed-size arrays (region_size[] and output_region[]) that are dimensioned to only 8 elements (valid indices 0-7). This causes out-of-bounds heap writes when the region value exceeds 7. The correct bitmask should be 0x7 to constrain the value to the valid 3-bit range (0-7).

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in the NPU_SET_IFM_REGION case handler at line 451: `st.ifm.region = param & 0x7f;` uses a bitmask of 0x7f (127) instead of 0x7 (7). This allows region index values up to 127 to be stored in st.ifm.region. Later, this region value is used as an array subscript in functions like dma_length() (line 190: `info->region_size[dma->region]`) and feat_matrix_length() (line 227: `info->region_size[fm->region]`), where region_size[] and output_region[] are fixed-size arrays dimensioned to only 8 elements (NPU_BASEP_REGION_MAX). This causes out-of-bounds heap writes. In contrast, other similar region handlers like NPU_SET_OFM_REGION (line 479), NPU_SET_IFM2_REGION (line 501), NPU_SET_WEIGHT_REGION (line 523), and NPU_SET_SCALE_REGION (line 526) correctly use the 0x7 bitmask. The fix is not present in this commit.
